claims.text: Explicit AIMD provides high-fidelity thermodynamic data at very high computational cost.
TOR-TILD improves throughput for elemental and binary systems.
TOR-TILD slows for complex multicomponent systems.
An ML interatomic potential can replace full AIMD sampling of both solid and liquid phases in fusion-property calculations.
The ML potential can capture vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling.
The training set will contain strategically selected AIMD configurations from solid and liquid states near fusion.
The training data will explicitly incorporate vibrational-entropy, anharmonic, and electron–vibration-coupling information.
On-the-fly retraining or active learning will be used to maintain accuracy near phase-transition conditions.
A potential learned from sparse but representative AIMD configurations can interpolate the relevant free-energy contributions.
This interpolation reduces the need for continuous AIMD sampling.
The proposed method will maintain AIMD-like fidelity for phase free energies and derived thermodynamic observables.
Errors relative to AIMD will be approximately no larger than the thermal-fluctuation uncertainty.
The proposed method will reduce computational cost by approximately 5–10 times relative to AIMD.
The proposed method will be significantly faster than TOR-TILD for multicomponent systems.
The initial validation domain is elemental and binary systems for which high-quality AIMD data are available.
The proposed temperature domain spans approximately 0.8–1.2 times the fusion temperature.
The method may not generalize accurately across phase boundaries if critical anharmonic or electron–vibration interactions are missed.
The method is falsified if phase free energies or derived fusion properties deviate from AIMD by more than 10%.
The method is falsified if its computational cost reduction is less than approximately fivefold relative to AIMD.
